anomalies.observed: Both alternative 0 Ω select resistors for each PWM channel are populated. R8 and R23 both join PWM1 (/NET0007) to bus pins 21 (/NET0042) and 19 (/NET0026). R1 and R12 both join PWM2 (/NET0011) to bus pins 22 (/NET0024) and 20 (/NET0002). This shorts distinct M5Stack GPIO bus signals together.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes R9–R12 as jumpers that select one bus pin per channel, with the other option left open. Shorting two different GPIO bus pins together would make them contend on the same node.

evidence.quote: R9–R12 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | Select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2)

anomalies.impact: Two GPIOs on the M5Stack bus are tied together for each servo channel. The core can drive contending outputs, and the intended single-pin selection is lost.

anomalies.observed: The MAX3485 B pin (U2.7) connects only to R3 (2.2k to GND) and R9 (2.2k to +3V3). It never reaches a servo signal pin. Only A (U2.6, via R19 0 Ω) reaches the servo bus at Net-(J11-Pin_3).
anomalies.expected: In the serial mode described by the spec, the MAX3485 A/B pair should drive the single shared servo bus. The B line should be tied to the servo signal node, not left as a bias divider that fights the driver.

evidence.quote: Serial mode (populate R13/R14 ...): J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 are tied together into one shared bus node and driven by U1 (MAX3485)

anomalies.impact: The transceiver drives only one side of the differential pair. The bias resistors fight its B output, which can corrupt serial servo communication.

anomalies.observed: R13 is 20k between the DE/RE node (Net-(Q3-C)) and GND, not a 0 Ω bridge. The only bridging jumper in the serial path is R14 (0 Ω).
anomalies.expected: The spec says R13 and R14 are both 0 Ω jumpers that bridge the two servo signal pins together ('Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo').

evidence.quote: R13, R14 | 0 Ω (jumpers) | When shorted, bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto the MAX3485 TTL bus

anomalies.impact: Serial-mode bridging depends on a single jumper instead of two, and the 20k part on the DE/RE line changes the assembly-option behaviour the spec describes. The spec's reference designators may not match this netlist, so this is a low-confidence finding.
